reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; nothing actionable is being asserted against the counterparty.

The cited text (§11.3 / p0132, p0137) is an acceptable-use enforcement and investigation right tied to breach of the Content/AUP warranties in §11.2(b), not a usage, licence or fee-verification audit of Customer. It grants no right of entry to Customer systems or records for measuring usage or charges, so the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, underpayment true-up) do not attach to it.

Absence of any audit right binding Customer is more favourable than the preferred position, so under the direction rule (do not flag a clause that benefits our party) treating this as compliant rather than 'missing' or a deviation is correct.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is adequately explained: there is no audit clause capable of carrying a frequency cap, so the regex miss is a phrasing/absence artefact rather than evidence of an unmet position.

Secondary observations (no confidentiality obligation on investigators, best-efforts notice in p0137, suspension/termination remedies left to other rules) are properly recorded in the rationale as file notes rather than raised as deviations or double-flagged.
